title: Choir and Salt Revisited
premise: Silas Brightwater, a mercenary whose god Veyra fell silent twelve years ago, has survived by selling harmless charms in the city of Correnholt, where magic is outlawed and the Choir of the Silent keeps watch. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin answering themselves, Silas discovers her own dormant oathmark burning again—and learns that Veyra's silence was not death but imprisonment, and that Silas's blood is the key to either freeing her or destroying what remains. Hunted by the Choir's Inquisitor and sheltered by a found family of smugglers, defrocked priests, and a runaway acolyte named Tamsin whom she comes to love, Silas must choose between breaking her oath to save the woman she loves and honoring it to prevent an ancient war from reigniting. In the end, Silas finds a third path: she gives up her own divine spark—the last fragment of Veyra—to seal the god away forever, saving Tamsin and the city at the cost of never hearing a god's voice again, but gaining a family that answers when she calls.
about_author: Yara Sterling is the pen name of a former choir singer turned fantasy novelist who grew up in coastal fishing towns where old superstitions still linger in the salt air. She writes stories about faith, found family, and the quiet heroism of people who were never meant to matter.

chapters.title: The Quiet Market
chapters.summary: Silas Brightwater sells a luck-charm to a fisherman's widow in Correnholt's gray market, hiding her oathmark beneath leather wraps. Her POV establishes twelve years of careful invisibility since her god went silent. The emotional beat is weary routine—until a child's desperate prayer in the alley is answered by light, and Silas feels her dead mark stir for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Bells Forgot
chapters.summary: Rumors spread of answered prayers across the city; the Choir of the Silent begins door-to-door searches. Silas, POV alternating briefly to Inquisitor Dain Merek hunting 'resonants,' burns her remaining charms and plans to flee. The emotional beat is dread: the life she built is ash, and the mark on her arm won't stop glowing.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Silas seeks out Brannoc Hale, an old smuggling contact who once ran relics for the faithful. He refuses her at first, then relents when his granddaughter's fever breaks after Silas instinctively prays aloud. POV Silas. The beat is reluctant hope—she can't outrun what she is, but maybe she can aim it.

chapters.title: The Acolyte Who Ran
chapters.summary: Silas catches a starving stowaway aboard Hale's barge: Tamsin, a runaway Choir acolyte who heard Veyra's name in a vision meant for Silas. Their first meeting is knives-then-truce. POV alternates between them. The beat is wary recognition—two people shaped by the same absent god, neither trusting the other yet.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: A flashback-heavy chapter: Silas recalls the mercenary company sworn to Veyra, the battle at the Saltfen where the god's voice cut out mid-prayer, and the comrades who died believing they'd been abandoned. POV Silas, told to Tamsin over a night watch. The beat is grief finally spoken aloud after a decade of swallowing it.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Merek interrogates a captured resonant and learns a marked survivor of the Saltfen company lives in Correnholt. His POV reveals he isn't a zealot but a man who lost his family to the god-wars and believes any returning divinity means slaughter. The beat is chilling sympathy—the antagonist's logic almost holds.

chapters.title: The Relic Road
chapters.summary: Hale's crew runs the river by night toward the Saltfen ruins, pursued by Choir patrol boats. Tamsin proves unexpectedly useful, singing a hymn that blinds their pursuers. POV Silas. The beat is found-family forming under fire—shared danger doing what trust alone could not.

chapters.title: Where the Voice Went Out
chapters.summary: At the Saltfen battlefield, Silas touches the stone altar and hears Veyra—not free, but imprisoned beneath it by the other gods for refusing to fight in the last war. Veyra names the price of release: a bearer's divine spark, freely given. POV Silas. The beat is terrible clarity: freedom for her god costs everything she has left.

chapters.title: Terms of an Old Oath
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Silas about hiding Veyra's terms; their argument cracks open into honesty about fear and faith. Meanwhile Merek's agents reach the ruins' edge. POV Tamsin primarily. The beat is intimacy through conflict—they stop being allies of convenience and start being each other's reason.

chapters.title: The Choir Closes In
chapters.summary: Merek raids the Saltfen camp; Hale is captured covering the others' escape. Silas uses her sparking power openly for the first time, revealing herself to save Tamsin. POV alternates Silas/Merek. The beat is sacrifice made real—her invisibility is gone forever, spent in one blazing moment.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Brannoc Hale
chapters.summary: Hale, in Choir cells, stalls Merek with half-truths while Silas's crew regroups in the undercity with a defrocked priest, Mother Ives, who knows how god-bonds can be transferred. POV Hale. The beat is stubborn courage—an ordinary man buying time with nothing but nerve.

chapters.title: Mother Ives Heresy
chapters.summary: Ives reveals a forbidden rite: a spark can be split among many bearers, diluting it—but no one has survived the splitting in three hundred years. Silas must decide whether to gamble her friends' lives. POV Silas. The beat is the weight of leadership—love makes every option monstrous.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Prayed For
chapters.summary: Tamsin confesses she didn't run from the Choir—she was cast out for praying to Veyra by name, and the vision she received was of Silas dying at the altar. POV Tamsin. The beat is devastating tenderness: she has known the ending all along and chose Silas anyway.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Company
chapters.summary: Merek offers Silas a deal via captured Hale's release: surrender herself and the city spares everyone she's touched. The crew fractures—some want her to take it, some to run, some to fight. POV Silas. The beat is the found family's first true wound, tested against duty's oldest trap.

chapters.title: Night of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Silas secretly agrees to Merek's terms to protect the others; Tamsin discovers the letter and intercepts the handoff, taking Silas's place at the meeting. POV alternates. The beat is love against duty made literal—each trying to be the sacrifice, neither willing to let the other burn.

chapters.title: Chains in the Cathedral Dark
chapters.summary: Tamsin is taken; Merek, shaken by her willingness to die for a mercenary, begins doubting his own certainty. Silas rallies the crew for an assault on the Choir's cathedral-prison. POV Merek primarily. The beat is the antagonist's crack—a man discovering his arithmetic forgot love.

chapters.title: The Rite of Splitting
chapters.summary: Before the rescue, Silas attempts Ives's rite with the crew as co-bearers so no single death can free or doom Veyra. It half-succeeds: the spark scatters, but Silas's connection to Veyra frays to threads. POV Silas. The beat is agonizing hope purchased with permanent loss.

chapters.title: Storming the Silent Choir
chapters.summary: The assault on the cathedral: Hale freed, Ives holding the doors with borrowed prayer, Tamsin rescued from the resonance engines the Choir built to siphon returning gods. Merek turns his blade on his own superiors rather than let Tamsin die. POV rotating across all four. The beat is every thread converging in fire.

chapters.title: Veyra Rising
chapters.summary: The resonance engines rupture and Veyra surges free—vast, wounded, and furious enough to reignite the god-war unless anchored. Silas realizes only a willing bearer fully given can hold her. POV Silas. The beat is the climax's terrible choice arriving exactly as Tamsin's vision foretold.

chapters.title: The Last Brightwater Prayer
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas walks into Veyra's rising light and gives her spark completely—not to free the god, but to bind her gently back to sleep, ending the threat forever. Veyra, understanding at last, blesses her instead of cursing her. POV Silas. The beat is transcendence through surrender—duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash and Song
chapters.summary: Correnholt buries its dead; the Choir reforms under Merek, now advocating coexistence instead of erasure. Silas survives, mortal and unmarked, deaf to the divine—but Tamsin's hand in hers is answer enough. POV Tamsin watching Silas wake. The beat is grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Choir and Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year later: Silas runs a market stall again—no charms now, just salt and bread—surrounded by Hale's grandchildren, Ives's rebuilt congregation, and Tamsin. When a stranger asks if she misses her god, she says the gods are quiet, but the people aren't. POV Silas. The beat is peace earned, not granted: survival's price paid, and worth it.
